The scaled dot-product attention formula is: 

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / √d_k) * V [2]

Where:
- Q is the query
- K is the key
- V is the value
- d_k is the dimensionality of the key
- K^T is the transpose of the key
- softmax is the softmax function 

This formula is used to compute the weighted sum of the values, where the weight assigned to each value is computed by a compatibility function of the query with the corresponding key [1]. The scaling factor of 1/√d_k is used to counteract the effect of large dot products, which can push the softmax function into regions where it has extremely small gradients [3, 4].

RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence differ in how they use retrieved documents to generate target tokens. 

RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate the complete sequence, treating it as a single latent variable [1]. 

In contrast, RAG-Token can predict each target token based on a different document [1]. This means that RAG-Token has more flexibility in choosing the information it uses to generate each token, whereas RAG-Sequence relies on a single document for the entire sequence.

This difference is also reflected in their decoding procedures, with RAG-Token using a standard beam decoder and RAG-Sequence requiring a different approach [4]. 

Additionally, the two models have different performance characteristics, with RAG-Token performing better with more retrieved documents, but at the expense of Bleu-1 score, whereas the effect is less pronounced for RAG-Sequence [2]. RAG-Sequence also generates more diverse text than RAG-Token [3]. 

However, in certain cases, such as sequence classification tasks with a target sequence of length one, RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token are equivalent [5].
